questions.q: What does the phrase 'A wild goose chase' mean?
questions.x: 'A wild goose chase' means: a futile search.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Everyone of the trainees / was given / a certificate.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'Everyone of the trainees'. 'Every one of' (two words) is correct when followed by 'of'.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: ANIMOSITY
questions.x: 'Animosity' is the opposite of 'Friendship'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Animosity'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A written record of what is discussed at a meeting'
questions.x: 'Minutes' means a written record of what is discussed at a meeting.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Jovial'.
questions.x: 'Jovial' is the opposite of 'Morose'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Jovial'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Superfluous'.
questions.x: 'Superfluous' means unnecessary. 'Essential' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: He has been working in this office ____ 2015.
questions.x: 'Since' is used with a point in time; 'for' with a period.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: METICULOUS
questions.x: 'Meticulous' means painstaking. 'Sloppy' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Each of the two / candidates were / interviewed separately.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'candidates were'. 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'was interviewed'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To be in hot water' mean?
questions.x: 'To be in hot water' means: to be in trouble.

questions.q: The phrase 'invisible capital' in the passage refers to:
questions.x: Answer: 'Trust'. The first sentence identifies trust as the invisible capital. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Trust is the invisible capital of any institution. A citizen who believes that a claim will be settled fairly and on time is more willing to follow rules, pay contributions and recommend the system to others. Each delay, each unexplained rejection, draws down this capital. Rebuilding it is slow, because people remember bad experiences longer than good ones. Institutions that publish clear timelines, explain their decisions and respond to grievances quickly earn trust that no advertisement can buy.

questions.q: According to the passage, why is rebuilding trust slow?
o: People remember bad experiences longer than good ones
questions.x: Answer: 'People remember bad experiences longer than good ones'. The passage gives this reason explicitly. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Trust is the invisible capital of any institution. A citizen who believes that a claim will be settled fairly and on time is more willing to follow rules, pay contributions and recommend the system to others. Each delay, each unexplained rejection, draws down this capital. Rebuilding it is slow, because people remember bad experiences longer than good ones. Institutions that publish clear timelines, explain their decisions and respond to grievances quickly earn trust that no advertisement can buy.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1939 session of the Indian National Congress held at Tripuri?
questions.x: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the 1939 Tripuri session — the session where Bose was re-elected defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

questions.q: The Ghadar Party was founded at San Francisco — this happened in the year:
questions.x: The Ghadar Party was founded at San Francisco in 1913. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Cornwallis. Zamindars became owners with a fixed revenue demand.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Cripps proposals were rejected by the Congress.
Reason (R): The proposals offered dominion status only after the war and allowed provinces to secede.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R gives the reasons for rejection.

questions.q: Who among the following founded the Indian Statistical Institute and is associated with the Second Five-Year Plan model?
questions.x: Correct answer: P. C. Mahalanobis. The ISI was founded in 1931 in Calcutta.

questions.q: The 'Nehru Report' (1928) was drafted by a committee headed by:
questions.x: It demanded dominion status; Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points (1929).

questions.q: Gopal Krishna Gokhale is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905).

questions.q: General Dyer ordered firing at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi). Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Home Rule Movement:
1. Tilak's League worked in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar.
2. Annie Besant's League covered the rest of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct.
The two leagues divided areas to avoid friction.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission (1946) consisted of:
o: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander
questions.x: Correct answer: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander. It proposed a three-tier federation and a Constituent Assembly.

questions.q: Sikkim's 'Mission Organic' made it, in 2016, India's first:
questions.x: Correct answer: Fully organic State. It was declared fully organic in January 2016.

questions.q: The 'Global Hunger Index' is published by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.x: 'Global Hunger Index' is brought out by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe.

questions.q: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour. It was earlier named after:
questions.x: Correct answer: Rajiv Gandhi. It was renamed in 2021.

questions.q: Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory mission, was placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1 in:
questions.x: Correct answer: January 2024. It was launched on 2 September 2023 by PSLV-C57.

questions.q: Which Indian film song won the Oscar for Best Original Song in 2023?
questions.x: Correct answer: Naatu Naatu (RRR). 'The Elephant Whisperers' won Best Documentary Short the same year.

questions.q: The 'Global Biofuels Alliance' was launched in 2023 with India and which other founding members among others?
questions.x: Correct answer: USA and Brazil. It was launched on the sidelines of the G20 Summit in New Delhi.

questions.q: Mark Carney became the Prime Minister of Canada in 2025, succeeding:
questions.x: He is a former Governor of the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 8 October?
questions.x: 8 October is Indian Air Force Day.

questions.q: In 2024, the WHO certified India as having eliminated which disease as a public health problem?
questions.x: India became the third country in the WHO South-East Asia region to do so.

questions.q: Navi Mumbai International Airport was inaugurated in:
questions.x: It is designed to decongest Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport.

questions.q: The Prime Minister is appointed by:
questions.x: Article 75(1); by convention the leader of the majority in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Article 143 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Protection of monuments and places of national importance
Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife
Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court (advisory jurisdiction)
Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.x: Article 143: Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court (advisory jurisdiction).

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "All-India Services"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 312.

questions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a Panchayati Raj structure of:
o: Two tiers — zila parishad and mandal panchayat
questions.x: Correct answer: Two tiers — zila parishad and mandal panchayat. It favoured the district as the first point of decentralisation.

questions.q: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described which Article as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.x: Article 32 provides the right to constitutional remedies.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission is a:
o: Statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
questions.x: Its chairperson is a former Chief Justice of India or a former Supreme Court judge.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body.
Reason (R): It is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every second year.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains why it is called permanent.

questions.q: The 'Model Code of Conduct' for elections is:
o: A set of guidelines evolved with consensus of parties, enforced by the Election Commission
questions.x: It is not statutory but is enforced through the EC's powers under Article 324.

questions.q: Department-related Standing Committees in Parliament were set up in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1993. There are 24 such committees examining demands for grants and bills.

questions.q: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.x: The 1935 Act had a limited franchise; adult suffrage came only with the Constitution.

questions.q: 'Stagflation' refers to a situation of:
o: High inflation along with stagnant growth and high unemployment
questions.x: Correct answer: High inflation along with stagnant growth and high unemployment. The 1970s oil shocks caused stagflation in many economies.

questions.q: The 'SARFAESI Act, 2002' empowers banks to:
o: Enforce security interest and recover dues without court intervention
questions.x: Correct answer: Enforce security interest and recover dues without court intervention. Asset reconstruction companies operate under it.

questions.q: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes provide:
o: Incentives on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India
questions.x: Correct answer: Incentives on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India. PLI schemes cover 14 sectors including electronics, pharma and auto.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. NITI Aayog is a constitutional body.
2. The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct.
NITI Aayog was created by a Cabinet resolution; it is neither constitutional nor statutory.

questions.q: 'Global Competitiveness Report' was historically published by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: World Economic Forum. The WEF also publishes the Global Gender Gap Report.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 20% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹100 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.2 = 5.
Total deposits = 100 × 5 = ₹500 crore (of which new credit = ₹400 crore).

questions.q: India is the world's largest producer of:
questions.x: India also leads in pulses production; China leads in wheat and rice production.

questions.q: The 'Skill India Mission' was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: July 2015. It includes Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana.

questions.q: SENSEX is the benchmark index of the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bombay Stock Exchange (30 stocks). NIFTY 50 is the NSE benchmark.

questions.q: 'Crowding out' refers to:
o: Reduction in private investment due to higher government borrowing raising interest rates
questions.x: Correct answer: Reduction in private investment due to higher government borrowing raising interest rates. It is a concern when fiscal deficits are high.

questions.q: Under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, the balance sheet is presented in the:
questions.x: Schedule III prescribes vertical formats for the balance sheet and statement of profit and loss.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹2,30,000 is depreciated at 25% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 2,30,000 × (0.75)^3 = ₹97,031.25.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹57,500.)

questions.q: Interest on capital allowed to the proprietor is recorded as:
o: Interest on Capital A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Capital A/c Dr. To Interest on Capital A/c
Interest on Capital A/c Dr. To Capital A/c
Cash A/c Dr. To Capital A/c
questions.x: Interest on capital is an expense for the business and is credited to the owner's capital.

questions.q: A trial balance can be prepared:
o: At any time, usually at the end of an accounting period
questions.x: Correct answer: At any time, usually at the end of an accounting period. It is a working statement that can be prepared whenever needed.

questions.q: Valuing closing inventory at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower, is an application of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Conservatism. Prudence prevents overstatement of assets and profit.

questions.q: A Limited Liability Partnership in India is governed by the:
questions.x: An LLP is a body corporate with separate legal entity and limited liability.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹3,000 at the end of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 6% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 3,000 = ₹36,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the end of each month = 5.5 months.
Interest = 36,000 × 6% × 5.5/12 = ₹990.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹45,000; Purchases ₹3,75,000; Purchase returns ₹1,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹4,24,500; Closing stock ₹20,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 45,000 + 3,75,000 − 1,000 + 3,000 − 20,000 = ₹4,02,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 4,24,500 − 4,02,000 = ₹22,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: The profits of a firm for the last 4 years were ₹26,000, ₹46,000, ₹76,000, ₹27,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
P and Q share profits in the ratio 2 : 3. They admit R for a 1/6 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
Debentures represent:
questions.x: Correct answer: Borrowed capital of the company. Debenture holders are creditors who receive interest.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹10,000, Debtors ₹95,000, Inventory ₹25,000, Prepaid expenses ₹7,500, Creditors ₹55,000, Bills payable ₹12,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹10,000. Its current ratio is:
Opening inventory is ₹30,000, closing inventory is ₹45,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹1,87,500. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (30,000 + 45,000) / 2 = ₹37,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 1,87,500 / 37,500 = 5 times.

questions.q: Credit purchase of furniture by a trader (not dealing in furniture) is recorded in the:
questions.x: The purchases book records only credit purchases of goods dealt in; assets go to the journal proper.

questions.q: Which factors does the Code on Wages specify for fixing minimum wages?
o: Skill category and arduousness of work, besides geographical area
Only the age and gender of the worker
The size of the employer's share capital
questions.x: Minimum wages are fixed taking into account skill (unskilled, semi-skilled, skilled, highly skilled), arduousness, geographical area and other factors — never gender.

questions.q: The Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 made which person responsible for providing welfare amenities if the contractor fails?
questions.x: If the contractor fails to provide canteens, rest rooms, drinking water etc., the principal employer must provide them and may recover the cost from the contractor.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise the right to protest peacefully but hold that there is no fundamental right to strike for government servants?
o: Kameshwar Prasad v. State of Bihar (1962)
Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950)
questions.x: Kameshwar Prasad struck down a blanket ban on demonstrations but upheld the ban on strikes by government servants.

questions.q: NITI Aayog's 2022 report 'India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy' projected the gig workforce to reach about how many by 2029–30?
questions.x: It estimated 77 lakh gig workers in 2020–21, rising to about 2.35 crore by 2029–30.

questions.q: The Central Industrial Relations Machinery (CIRM), headed by the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), is responsible for:
o: Prevention and settlement of industrial disputes and enforcement of labour laws in the central sphere
questions.x: CIRM, set up in 1945, is an attached office of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

questions.q: Which new right did the OSH Code give to every employee irrespective of the size of the establishment covered by it?
questions.x: Every employer must issue an appointment letter to each employee on appointment.

questions.q: 'Lay-off' differs from 'retrenchment' in that lay-off is:
o: A temporary inability to give employment, with the worker remaining on the rolls
questions.x: Lay-off is temporary (due to shortage of material, power, breakdown, etc.); retrenchment is termination for reasons other than disciplinary punishment.

questions.q: A worker who worked 200 days in the previous calendar year in a factory claims annual leave. Under the OSH Code, the worker:
o: Is not eligible because 240 days are needed
Is eligible only if a woman
Is eligible, since the eligibility is 180 days of work
Is eligible only after five years
questions.x: Eligibility is 180 days; at 1 day per 20 days worked, the worker earns 10 days of leave.

questions.q: The Working Journalists and Other Newspaper Employees Act was enacted in:
questions.x: It provided conditions of service and wage boards for journalists; now subsumed in the OSH Code.

questions.q: ILO Recommendation No. 202 (2012) is concerned with:
questions.x: R202 asks states to establish basic social security guarantees — access to essential health care and basic income security across the life cycle.

questions.q: A '360-degree' performance appraisal collects feedback from:
o: Supervisors, peers, subordinates, self and sometimes customers
questions.x: Correct answer: Supervisors, peers, subordinates, self and sometimes customers. Multi-rater feedback gives a rounded view of performance.

questions.q: The National Career Service portal, launched in 2015, primarily provides:
o: Job matching, career counselling and skill information
questions.x: NCS, run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, connects job seekers and employers and runs Model Career Centres.

questions.q: The IR Code excludes from the definition of 'worker' a person employed in a supervisory capacity drawing wages exceeding (or as notified):
questions.x: Supervisory employees earning above ₹18,000 a month (or such higher amount as notified) are not 'workers'.

questions.q:
Match the labour forum with its function under the IR Code:
Forum:
A. Grievance Redressal Committee
B. Works Committee
C. Conciliation Officer
D. Industrial Tribunal
Function:
1. Mediates industrial disputes
2. Promotes amity and good relations
3. Resolves individual workers' grievances
4. Adjudicates industrial disputes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Grievance Redressal Committee) → 3 (Resolves individual workers' grievances); B (Works Committee) → 2 (Promotes amity and good relations); C (Conciliation Officer) → 1 (Mediates industrial disputes); D (Industrial Tribunal) → 4 (Adjudicates industrial disputes).
Each forum has a distinct role from grievance resolution to adjudication.

questions.q: Aggregators employing gig and platform workers must contribute to social security at a rate of:
o: 1–2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount paid or payable to such workers
questions.x: Section 114 of the Code on Social Security prescribes this contribution, to be notified by the Central Government.

questions.q: Wage Boards in India, such as the Majithia Wage Board, were set up to recommend wages for:
o: Working journalists and non-journalist newspaper employees
questions.x: Statutory wage boards for journalists functioned under the Working Journalists Act; the Majithia Board's recommendations were upheld by the Supreme Court in 2014.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹14,500 and pensionable service of 20 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (14,500 × 20) / 70 = ₹4,143.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): PAYG pension systems come under stress when populations age.
Reason (R): Ageing reduces the number of contributors per pensioner.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A: fewer workers support more retirees.

questions.q: 'Atal Bimit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana' under ESIC provides:
o: Cash relief to insured persons rendered unemployed
questions.x: ABVKY (2018) gives unemployment allowance; during COVID the relief was enhanced to 50% of average earnings for up to 90 days.

questions.q: Gratuity for an employee with last drawn wages of ₹26,000 and 10 years of service is:
Form 10D under the EPF schemes is used to claim:
questions.x: Correct answer: Monthly pension under EPS 1995. Form 10D is the pension claim form; Form 5IF is for EDLI.

questions.q: Child Care Leave for women Central Government employees is available for a maximum of:
questions.x: Women employees (and single male parents) may avail up to two years (730 days) of child care leave.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹16,000 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,000 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 20%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,000) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(16,000, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 20% = ₹16,800. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: In computing gratuity, why is 26 used as the divisor for monthly wages?
o: It represents the number of working days in a month
It is the statutory retirement age divided by 2
It represents fortnights in a year
questions.x: Monthly wages ÷ 26 gives a day's wage (assuming four weekly rest days).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Members of the EDLI Scheme do not contribute to it.
Reason (R): The EDLI Scheme is financed by employer contribution and administered by EPFO.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A — the scheme is wholly employer-funded.

questions.q: The EPF 'Electronic Challan-cum-Return' (ECR) is used by employers to:
o: Remit contributions and file the monthly return together
questions.x: ECR combines payment and member-wise return of wages and contributions.

questions.q: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY), launched in 2008, was originally implemented by the Ministry of:
questions.x: RSBY was a Labour Ministry scheme for BPL families before moving to the Health Ministry and PM-JAY.

questions.q: The maximum monthly EPS contribution from the employer, given the ₹15,000 wage ceiling, is:
Which of the following is an example of an application software?
questions.x: Correct answer: MS Word. Operating systems, drivers and firmware are system software.

questions.q: India's first satellite, launched in 1975 by the Soviet Union, was:
questions.x: Correct answer: Aryabhata. It was named after the ancient astronomer.

questions.q: The sky appears blue because of:
o: Scattering of light (shorter wavelengths scatter more)
Absorption of red light by air
questions.x: Correct answer: Scattering of light (shorter wavelengths scatter more). This is Rayleigh scattering.

questions.q:
Consider the following devices:
1. Router
2. Switch
3. Modem
4. Printer
How many of the above are networking devices?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Router, switch and modem are networking devices; a printer is an output peripheral.

questions.q: The 'CC' field in an email is used to:
o: Send a copy to additional recipients visible to all
questions.x: Correct answer: Send a copy to additional recipients visible to all. BCC (blind carbon copy) hides recipients from each other.

questions.q: Soap removes oily dirt because soap molecules:
o: Have a water-loving head and an oil-loving tail that form micelles
questions.x: Correct answer: Have a water-loving head and an oil-loving tail that form micelles. Micelles trap oil and are washed away.

questions.q: The splitting of white light into its component colours by a prism is called:
questions.x: Rainbows form by dispersion, refraction and internal reflection in raindrops.

questions.q: A 'compiler' translates:
o: An entire high-level program into machine code before execution
One line at a time during execution
questions.x: Correct answer: An entire high-level program into machine code before execution. An interpreter translates and executes line by line.

questions.q: DNA is mainly found in the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Nucleus. Small amounts are also present in mitochondria and chloroplasts.

questions.q: Which storage device has no moving parts?
questions.x: Correct answer: Solid State Drive. SSDs use flash memory and are faster than HDDs.

questions.q: A sphygmomanometer is used to measure:
questions.x: Sphygmomanometer: Blood pressure.

questions.q: The chemical symbol for sodium is:
questions.x: From the Latin 'natrium'. Potassium is K (kalium).

questions.q: The average weight of 9 parcels is 43 kg. When one more parcel is added, the average becomes 44 kg. The weight of the new parcel is:
questions.x:
Old total = 9 × 43 = 387 kg. New total = 10 × 44 = 440 kg.
New parcel = 440 − 387 = 53 kg.
Shortcut: new value = new average + (increase × old count) = 44 + 1 × 9 = 53 kg.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 4 : 3. After 10 years, the ratio will become 38 : 31. What is P's present age?
What simple interest will ₹5,500 earn in 5 years at 4% per annum?
Asha can digitise a set of records in 14 days and Bhavna in 84 days. They start together, but Asha leaves after 6 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 6 days = 6 × (1/14 + 1/84) = 6/12 = 1/2.
Remaining = 1/2, done by Bhavna alone in 1/2 × 84 = 42 days.
Total = 6 + 42 = 48 days.

questions.q: There are 59 names in a row of candidates. Imran's name is 22nd from the top. What is its position from the bottom?
questions.x: Position from bottom = Total − position from top + 1 = 59 − 22 + 1 = 38.

questions.q: A train 280 m long running at 72 km/h crosses a platform in 33 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Distance covered in 33 s = 660 m = train + platform.
Platform = 660 − 280 = 380 m.

questions.q:
New establishments registered — 2019: 180  |  2020: 160  |  2021: 145  |  2022: 165  |  2023: 145.
What is the percentage change from 2019 to 2023?
questions.x:
Change = 145 − 180 = -35 on a base of 180 (earlier year).
% change = -35/180 × 100 = -19.44% → 19.44% decrease.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 117, 78, 273 and 76.
questions.x: 78, 273, 117 are all multiples of 13; 76 is not. Hence 76 is the odd one out.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, ?
questions.x: Terms are 2²+1, 3²+1, … so the next is 7² + 1 = 50.

questions.q: A invests ₹20,000 for the whole year and B invests ₹20,000 after 7 months. If the annual profit is ₹32,300, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 20,000×12, B: 20,000×5 → 12 : 5.
B's share = 5/17 × 32,300 = ₹9,500.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows a discount of 12% on the marked price. His gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 125.

questions.q: Meena starts from point O and walks 23 km towards South, then turns left and walks 9 km, then turns left and walks 18 km, and finally turns left and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -23 +18 = -5 km → 5 km South.
East–West: +9 -21 = -12 km → 12 km West.
Distance = √(12² + 5²) = 13 km, towards South-West.

questions.q: At what time between 5 and 6 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.x:
At 5:00 the minute hand is 25 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To coincide it must gain 25 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 25 × 60/55 = 300/11 minutes = 27 3/11 minutes past 5.

questions.q: What is the least number which, when divided by 20, 9, 24, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.x: Required number = LCM(20, 9, 24) + 3 = 360 + 3 = 363.
